attempted_claim: Let F=F(a,b,c,d,e) be free of rank 5 and let phi in Aut(F) be a->b, b->c, c->ab, d->ea, e->ed. Let F'=<a,b,c> and phi'=phi|_{F'}. Let G = F semidirect_phi Z and Gamma = F' semidirect_{phi'} Z be the mapping tori. Prove that Gamma and G are not quasi-isometric.
decisive_failure: No proof excludes homologically trivial periodic classes for phi-prime or phi, so the hyperbolicity status of Gamma and G is unestablished; integral homology coincides (H_1=Z for both), leaving no elementary separating invariant; the bounded periodic-class screens are evidence only, not proof; the JSJ/lamination quasi-isometry-invariance machinery for the nested pair was not proved; exact integer computations (primitivity, Bareiss determinants, preimage identities) are reproducible checks recorded in WORKLOG.md.
